title: No formal teacher: Chif, Joe Howard and Paul Rozier
summary: Punch says he learned notes from Chif, intonation and fingering from Joe Howard and marching from Paul Rozier.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well when you started off with a teacher did the teacher make you practice much? Well guess how that

happened. I didn't have no teacher. Not at noon. And the element we went rehearsal two hours in the morning and two hours in the evening. Where Chip, like I tell you, Chip used to sit right side me and show me a lot of notes see. I didn't know. I ain't gonna lie. I didn't know. But I would anything he'd tell me I remembered. I don't care how long up until the day I can remember anything he told me. Told me what an eight note was, a quarter note was, and how many notes was in the bar and I remember all that see. I wasn't hard to catch on. And Joe Howard he showed me more tonation and fingering and things like that see. That's the most he showed me. A whole lot of that. And old Paul Rozier from Barley-Zellman, Louisiana, he showed me a whole lot too. That's where I went in the Army anyway. I was going to play the blues. That's all I could play the blues. Well he was quite a musician but he didn't play no jazz or nothing but marching. You know them marching and things. That's all they played.
Well what are some of the different things that they taught you about tonation and fingering?

Oh? Well Joe Howard would tell me if I hit, what's the male I'm playing, hit it solid see. Like I said. About stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like If you make a bed, be loud enough for everybody to understand it. He's telling me all that. But old Chip, I used to walk along right side and hang a blow, and playing, he put on a finger, I'm putting on a finger too. What's going on? Chip said you can't make it like that.
